== Basics == Fletching can be used to make bows and arrows. Combines are made in a [[Fletching Kit]]. Almost everything you will ever need for fletching can be bought from a merchant. While the number of fletching components is relatively small, they can be combined in a multitude of ways, with over 216 arrow combinations and 63 bow combinations. Most of these combinations can result in identical stats, and therefore you should note this page focuses on the cheapest versions. The main reason to do fletching is that making your own arrows is better than buying the merchant versions especially since in EQL you can upgrade arrows by merging. You should plan on making as many as 1024 arrows to max out a given arrow to +10. The maximum range of a shot is calculated by adding the bow's range and the arrow's range. == Fletching Advice == '''Tips on Becoming a Master Fletcher by Siobhan, with edits and addendum for Everquest Live by Jokon''' The nice thing about fletching is that you’re basically making two objects, bows and arrows, over and over again. That makes it very easy to figure out the relative difficulty of making a particular item. Basically, the higher the quality of your supplies, i.e. the more expensive they are, the more difficult they are to work with. If you seem to be getting a lot of failures with a particular type of arrow or bow, try downgrading one or more of your components to something cheaper. Please note that there isn’t a direct correspondence between the cost of arrows and bows and their relative difficulty. Rough hickory bows will be trivial to make long before you’re able to manufacture arrows costing several gp apiece. When making bows, the bow staff determines base damage, range, and delay. Your string modifies this. The better quality the string, the less damage the bow does but the shorter the delay. This means that a hickory bow with a linen string will do more damage than a hickory bow with a silk string, but the bow with the silk string will be faster. Whittling knives and planing tools decrease delay even more but reduce damage as well. Cams also reduce delay and damage. Basically, the more stuff you put on the bow the faster it will get. It will also hit for less damage, but typically you always see an overall improvement in your ratio. As for arrows, the better the arrowhead, the more damage the arrow will do. Same for shafts, the better quality the shaft is, the more damage the arrow does. Feathers modify range and damage. Round cut feathers will give your arrow a base range of 50. Parabolic cut feathers will increase the base range to 100. Shield cut feathers will reduce base range to 0 but increase the base damage of the arrow. Nocks modify the base range of the arrow so that the smaller, i.e. better, the nock the greater the range of the arrow. Finally, when practicing to raise your general skill level always work on arrows instead of bows. Arrows are far cheaper to make than bows so your mistakes will be far less costly and you can make more attempts for the same amount of money. You will want to make bows to use in the early levels but for the most part, practice on arrows. --Siobhan, Tunare Server --Jokon, Rivervale Server == Level Up Guide == If you're just looking to level up Fletching you can follow these charts for the quickest and cheapest way. If you want to know more about the details about how to make custom arrows and bows you can find those details further below. '''Dexterity, Intelligence, or Wisdom: whichever is higher governs your chance to gain skill increases.''' The trivial of any arrow is determined by the highest trivial out of all 4 components. '''The absolute cheapest''' way to level fletching is to use just the single component which will yield an arrow with a high enough trivial to raise your fletching, and the '''cheapest''' things available for the other 3 components. However, this will usually lead to an arrow with terrible stats. If you have extra coin and plan to use the arrows upgrade first to [[Several Parabolic Cut Fletchings|Parabolic Fletching +50 Range]] then [[Small Groove Nocks|Small Nocks +50 Range]] then [[Bundled Bone Arrow Shafts|Bone Shafts +1 Dmg]]. ('''Note:''' Gnome Necro with 228 INT, 56 CHA went from 1-162 skill in about 265pp total and 163-182 skill in about another 350pp. So grab 600pp at that INT and CHA to get the job done easily and have some money left over. This will be the fast track so you can buy stacks and move quickly.)

=== Surefall Fletching for Everquest Live by Jokon === One of the easiest ways to become a master fletcher is to A) Worship Karana and B) use Qaelin Hailstorm to craft lots of arrows. Note this guide is specifically for fletching from 203 onwards; prior to that skill level it's far cheaper to use traditional fletching components. Additionally, you're going to have to get blacksmithing up to 188 or so if you want to be truly self-sufficient; this is the minimum skill required for making the [[Steel Arrowheads]] that are required. To quickly summarize: # Worship Karana as your active deity # Have 203 Fletching and 188 [[Blacksmithing]] If you can fill those requirements, it's time to talk to [[Qaelin Hailstorm]]. You need to get the [[Mark of Karana]] from him which is a necessary component for all meaningful subcombines in Surefall Fletching. The keyword is "I need a mark" - however, as of May 26, 2026 you need to say this while next to Qaelin Hailstorm but without targeting him. When determining final arrow statistics add each component's affects on damage and range. Note: range can never go below 5.
The trivial is simply the highest trivial value of the four components.

== Bow Details == Bows consist of a '''bow staff''' and '''string''' with optional '''cams''' and '''tools''' if the base wood allows.
Just like with arrows the final statistics (Damage, Range, Delay) are dependent each component.
While the trivial is determined by the highest trivial of any single part.
Regardless of '''success''' or '''failure''' the staff, string, and cams are lost but tools will always be returned. '''Making your first bow''' String is required for all bows. Choices include[[Hemp Twine | Hemp]],[[Linen String | Linen]], and[[Silk String | Silk]]. Hemp is the simplest to work with, and yields highest damage but longest delay. Linen and Silk are progressively more complex to work with, and provide progressively lower damage and delay. Additionally you can use a tool ([[Whittling Blade]] or [[Planing Tool]]) and/or 1-2 [[Standard Bow Cam]] but you are limited in what you can used based on what the bow staff will allow them. The simpler tool choice is the [[Whittling Blade| Blade]], which yields a Carved bow. The more advanced tool is the [[Planing Tool |Plane]], which yields a Shaped bow. The use of 1 cam yields a 1-cam bow and two cams yields a compound bow. As a general rule, you'll find that adding more components to your bow will reduce both damage and delay, but the overall ratio of the bow will be better (meaning higher overall DPS).

=== Restringing Your Bow === It is possible to change the string on the basic crafted bows listed on the above chart. This allows the discriminating archer to change out bow strings and modify slightly his/her bow characteristics according to the situation at hand. To change bow strings, place a completed bow into the fletching kit along with the new string, and hit combine. The result will be the same bow with only the string changed. The old string is not recovered. Changing strings becomes trivial at skill 16, but appears '''never fail''', offering an interesting alternative to gaining skill up to skill 16. == Vendors ==
